The first exact-head CI run caught a test fixture type mismatch, not a runtime failure: the progress-narrator fixture lacked the explicitly undefined `authProfileId` field returned by utility selection. Fixed in fa9e3e9b91c8b8138a9f9c6e9f508c7b7a117f14. The runtime patch is unchanged.

Failure evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33575224839/job/100077850753 (`TS2741` in `progress-narrator-model.test.ts:12`). The fixture correction passed the required uncommitted autoreview at its default P0 threshold; exact-head CI is now running at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33576684361.

The 203-test before/after verification remains the behavioral evidence. Live native-CLI proof and the remaining checks are still in progress; this is not yet a ready-to-merge claim.

Both requested Rank-up moves are addressed in the current candidate, `5ff350f21705deb1a8b1972a3420c5a15bb9a433`.

The shared utility-preparation owner now supplies `outputTextPolicy: "strict-visible"`, preserving the observer's existing empty-output JSON retry and the other utility callers' visible-text fallback. The real helper is exercised by `publishes a digest from a runtime-owned %s utility completion after empty output without API auth` for both legacy `claude-cli` and canonical `anthropic` selections. Before that production change, both cases failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`; afterward all 76 focused tests across observer, titles, narrator, and isolated completion passed. No timeout or assertion was weakened.

Native proof also passed through installed Claude Code 2.1.233 using the real utility selector and isolated runtime. An isolated API-key profile was forwarded to the native CLI; the operator's login and Gateway were untouched. Gateway-equivalent runtime publication preceded the calls. A host-process fetch trap rejected any direct `api.anthropic.com` request. These are actual subprocess results, not model mocks:

```json
{"ref":"claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5","owner":{"kind":"cli","id":"claude-cli"},"text":"utility-runtime-ok","directProviderRequests":0,"deadlineMs":10000,"durationMs":1956}
{"ref":"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5","owner":{"kind":"cli","id":"claude-cli"},"text":"utility-runtime-ok","directProviderRequests":0,"deadlineMs":10000,"durationMs":2057}
```

Each native turn used an empty tool surface and a new isolated session. Canonical configuration attached `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`; the legacy case retained the explicit CLI owner through canonicalization. Both earlier warmup calls also passed (18,885 ms and 2,076 ms with 20-second warmup budgets). The production observer's 10-second deadline is unchanged. This proves native dispatch and host HTTP exclusion, not subscription-login authentication or end-to-end Gateway/UI delivery. The observer default-adapter regression separately proves digest broadcast and that the synthetic native-auth marker never reaches direct completion. A further real observer-digest probe is in progress and is not counted as passing evidence here.

Required uncommitted autoreview: `autoreview scoped-clean: no accepted/actionable findings in the selected Git scope and priority` (default P0 threshold, exit 0). Plugin SDK API comparison reports no changes. Exact-head CI and final branch review are still running; this comment does not assert readiness before those gates finish.

Native observer-digest proof passed on `ec74dc6ef08d525677175ce313b71c2320305373` with installed Claude Code 2.1.233. This exercised `createSessionObserverCompletion`, its real default preparation/completion adapters, native CLI subprocess execution, and the production strict JSON validator. It used synthetic activity notes, temporary state, and an isolated API-key profile; it did not touch the operator's subscription login or running Gateway.

```json
{"ref":"claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6","owner":{"kind":"cli","id":"claude-cli"},"digest":{"headline":"Investigating a boundary case in the parser","health":"on-track","planProgress":{"completed":1,"total":3}},"directProviderRequests":0,"deadlineMs":10000,"durationMs":6053,"attempts":1}
{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","owner":{"kind":"cli","id":"claude-cli"},"digest":{"headline":"Reviewing synthetic parser implementation","health":"on-track","planProgress":{"completed":1,"total":3}},"directProviderRequests":0,"deadlineMs":10000,"durationMs":4663,"attempts":1}
```

Both returned bounded assessment text as well. The canonical model had `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`; the legacy reference retained the same execution owner. The probe rejected any direct host `api.anthropic.com` request, verified controller cleanup, and exited 0. Native CLI setup was warmed before measuring the unchanged 10-second observer deadline. Broadcast, persistence fencing, and lifecycle behavior are covered by the observer tests, not claimed as live UI proof.

Named follow-up: native Haiku 4.5 sometimes returns fenced JSON despite the strict format instruction; the existing second attempt can then exceed the 10-second budget. The observer prompt now explicitly forbids outer fences, but the Haiku rerun still exhibited that behavior, so this is not claimed fixed. It is separate from runtime/auth routing: the CLI executes successfully, the strict parser rejects the output, and the existing observer failure path records a non-outcome instead of sending the native-auth marker as an HTTP credential. Structured-output enforcement across runtime owners deserves a separate capability-level change; this PR does not weaken parsing, extend deadlines, add retries, or add configuration.

Final focused rerun: 36 observer tests passed. The previous focused run passed 76 tests and the broader Linux Testbox run passed 203. `pnpm check:changed` passed. Final branch autoreview exited 0: `autoreview scoped-clean: no accepted/actionable findings in the selected Git scope and priority` (default P0 threshold).
